title: Deep Reinforcement Learning from Human Preferences
authors: P. Christiano, J. Leike, T. Brown, M. Martic, S. Legg, D. Amodei
before: Reinforcement learning needed a hand-written reward function.
problem: Many goals are easy to judge and hard to specify. You know good behaviour when you see it.
breakthrough: Learn a reward model from human comparisons between pairs of behaviours, then optimise against it.
why: The whole alignment stack starts here. InstructGPT, ChatGPT and Claude are this method applied to language.
next: Ziegler applied it to language models in 2019, then summarisation, then instruction following.
inherits: Reward models learned from preference comparisons.
